merger_description:
Golden Energy and Resources Pte Ltd (**GEAR**) and M Resources Pty Ltd (**M Resources**) (together, the **Consortium**) propose to acquire the assets of the insolvent Tahmoor Colliery (**Tahmoor**). Tahmoor is a coal mine in the Illawarra region of NSW. The relevant assets include the mining rights, plant and equipment, real estate and a 16.67% equity interest in Port Kembla Coal Terminal Limited.

The acquiring entity, Golden M Tahmoor Coal Holdings Pty Ltd, will ultimately be owned 70% by GEAR (or related entities) and 30% by M Resources (or related entities / persons i.e. Matthew Lattimore).

GEAR and M Resources are part of an existing consortium, GM3, which operates the Appin and Dendrobium coal mines in the Illawarra region (through Illawarra Coal Holdings Pty Ltd) and has an existing minority interest in the Port Kembla Coal Terminal (together, the **GM3 Assets**). GEAR has a 51% economic interest in the GM3 Assets and M Resources has 7%.

GEAR is a Singaporean based resources company. Its activities in Australia involve gold mining and metallurgical (coking) coal production, through the GM3 Assets and a 59% shareholding in Stanmore Resources Limited (**Stanmore**), which produces coal in Queensland.

M Resources is an Australian based coal trader and logistics provider. It has interests in various businesses which service coal mines, including Mastermyne Limited, One Rail Australia Holdings Limited, Merald, M Critical Minerals and Stanmore. None of these businesses interact with mines in the Illawarra region except for the GM3 mines.

Tahmoor produces coking coal and small amounts of thermal coal for domestic and export customers. Tahmoor has been inoperative since late 2024 and is in liquidation.

determination_table_content.details:
Golden Energy and Resources Pte Ltd (GEAR) and M Resources Pty
Ltd (M Resources) (together, the Consortium) propose to acquire,
via a jointly owned special purpose vehicle, the assets of the
insolvent Tahmoor Colliery (Tahmoor) (together, the Parties).
Tahmoor is a coal mine in the Illawarra region of NSW.
The relevant assets include the mining rights, plant and equipment,
real estate and a 16.67% equity interest in Port Kembla Coal
Terminal Limited.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquiring entity, Golden M Tahmoor Coal Holdings Pty Ltd, will
ultimately be owned 70% by GEAR (or related entities) and 30% by M
Resources (or related entities / persons).
GEAR and M Resources are part of an existing consortium, GM3,
which operates the Appin and Dendrobium coal mines in the
Illawarra region (through Illawarra Coal Holdings Pty Ltd) and has an
existing minority interest in the Port Kembla Coal Terminal (together,
the GM3 Assets). GEAR has a 51% economic interest in the GM3
Assets and M Resources has 7%.
GEAR is a Singaporean based resources company. Its activities in
Australia involve gold mining and metallurgical (coking) coal
production, through the GM3 Assets and a 59% shareholding in
Stanmore Resources Limited (Stanmore), which produces coal in
Queensland.
M Resources is an Australian based coal trader and logistics
provider. It has interests in various businesses which service coal
mines, including Mastermyne Limited, One Rail Australia Holdings
Limited, Merald, M Critical Minerals and Stanmore. None of M
Resources businesses interact with mines in the Illawarra region
except for the GM3 Assets.
Tahmoor produces coking coal and small amounts of thermal coal
for domestic and export customers. Tahmoor has been inoperative
since late 2024 and is in liquidation.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
The Parties overlap in the production and supply of thermal and
coking coal in the Illawarra region. GM3 and Tahmoor, before it
ceased operating, both supplied coal to export customers as well as
BlueScope Steel Limited (BlueScope), based in Port Kembla.
Historically, GM3 also acquired coking coal from Tahmoor to supply
export customers.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties, and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Acquisition is unlikely to have an adverse impact on the only
domestic consumer of coking coal, taking into account long-
term supply arrangements being put in place and export
customers of coking coal have a range of alternative options.
• The aggregation in the supply of thermal coal resulting from the
Acquisition is low, and both domestic and export customers
have a range of alternative suppliers of thermal coal post-
acquisition.
• The merged entity is unlikely to have the ability and incentive to
foreclose rivals’ access to the Port Kembla Coal Terminal given
the merged entity would not have a controlling interest post-
acquisition.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
